tagline.text: Terraced paddies and a waterfall in a quiet mountain village of eastern Bohol

location.label: Location
location.text: Barangay Cadapdapan, Candijay, eastern Bohol, about 97–100 km from Tagbilaran

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱600~2,500 (per person, based on a day trip from Tagbilaran including transport, entrance fees and meals)

children.text: Cadapdapan is a mountain village in Candijay, eastern Bohol, where rice terraces fed by water from the upper reaches of a stream wind around a farm restaurant. It is a countryside route that you can combine in one day with nearby Can-umantad Falls and Canawa Cold Spring.
Cadapdapan is one of the 21 barangays of the municipality of Candijay on the eastern side of Bohol, a mountain village reached from Candijay's town center by a
15–30 minute
motorcycle ride uphill. Candijay is about
97 km
from Tagbilaran and about
105 km

from Panglao. Wikipedia lists the hinterland rice terraces of Candijay in the barangays of Tambongan, Canawa, Cadapdapan, Tubod and Abihilan. Locals consider the Cadapdapan paddies the most visually appealing terraces in Bohol, so they draw the most visitors. One travel writer candidly notes that the terraces are not as high or grand as the famous Cordillera terraces in northern Luzon. So rather than expecting a grand view, plan on a relaxed walk along country paths and paddy dikes.

The farm is the heart of the trip. The terraces spread around a private property called Eleuterio's Farm and its restaurant, and they are reportedly irrigated by the headwaters of the Cadapdapan River. At the restaurant in the middle of the paddies you can have a drink or a meal and leave your bag while you walk the dikes. One blogger wrote that the place is remote and almost empty of people, with small paths winding in several directions through the terraces and a few houses scattered among them. Other visitors say the dirt roads are many and the signs few, so it is hard to find on a first visit; save the exact map pin ahead of time or get help from a local motorcycle driver. After heavy rain the dirt road turns muddy, so choose a day without rain if you can. The Bohol tourism listing treats the terraces as a free site, but many reports say small fees are collected by the barangay and the private owners, so prepare cash.
The terraces alone can make half a day feel long, so most visitors combine them with nearby Can-umantad Falls. Walking down from the farm takes about
15 minutes
, and it is a few minutes by motorcycle. The two-tier falls drop about
60 ft
in total, with the main cascade about
45 ft

, and are described as the highest in Bohol. The pool below is a deep greenish-blue basin said to be good for swimming. A newly built paved access road exists but is very steep, so some travelers prefer to walk down. It is said that you can visit all three places, including Canawa Cold Spring, in one day.

This article is based on travel accounts from 2019 to the present and on Bohol tourism material. Fees, road conditions and opening hours change often, so follow on-site notices first. Wikipedia's Candijay page says Can-umantad Falls is still being developed and does not list the Cadapdapan terraces as a separate attraction. In other words, this is not a developed park but a place where travelers quietly pass through paddies and a farm where residents work. Staying on the paths without stepping on the paddy edges, and asking residents' permission before taking photos, is good for both the village and visitors.

Small paths run between paddies laid out in tiers along the hillside. In the dry season after harvest the fields are tidied and the paths are good for walking, and one traveler recommended November to March. The condition of the rice differs by season, so ask locally before you visit.

blocks.title: Restaurant in the middle of the paddies

children.text: At the restaurant in the middle of the terraces you can have drinks and a simple meal, and visitors report that staff do not mind if you leave your bag while you walk. A small separate fee may be charged at the gate to the restaurant.
About
15 minutes

of walking down from the farm brings you to the two-tier waterfall. Its total drop is described as about 60 ft, with the main cascade about 45 ft. The pool below is greenish-blue and deep, and said to be good for swimming. It is slippery, so bring suitable shoes.
A clear, cold spring in Barangay Canawa that can be combined with the falls in a day. It is a nice place to cool your feet and rest on a hot day.
The motorcycle road from the Candijay town center to the terraces is mostly dirt and is said to turn slippery with mud on rainy days. Local drivers know the road well, which makes it safer.

blocks.title: Other things to see in Candijay

children.text: Around Candijay you are told of the Kawasihan islet sandbar in Panas, the Danicop gorge brook in Cambane, Kantaligsok Peak in Tugas, and the mangrove forest in Panadtaran, where the PAMAS community group runs a mangrove adventure tour. The mangroves of Cogtong Bay in front of Candijay are described as the most diverse in Bohol, with 32 of the Philippines' 47 mangrove and associate species. Layog Caves in Luan, Sangat Cave in Tambongan, Ilaja Cave in Panas and the man-made Boongon lake are also mentioned as tourism candidates, but most are still being developed, so check locally.

blocks.title: A day in a farming town

children.text: After walking the paddies and the falls you can rest and have lunch in Candijay's town center. The town had about 30,000 residents in 2024, and the Poblacion is its largest barangay. Its parish church, dedicated to Saint Joseph, is listed with a feast day on May 19.
Candijay lies along the route to the eastern coast around Anda, so travelers going to Anda from Panglao or Tagbilaran on an overnight trip often stop here on the way.
Take a bus or van bound for Candijay, Ubay or Jagna from the Dao terminal in Tagbilaran.
Get off in Candijay town or Lungsoda-an and find a motorcycle driver.
Ride up to Cadapdapan, register at the entrance and walk the dikes.
Rest or have lunch at the farm restaurant.
Walk down to Can-umantad Falls to look around or swim.
Move on to Canawa Cold Spring or the town center.
Return to Tagbilaran by bus or van.

The last bus may leave early in the afternoon, so check the time and decide your return trip in advance. If you walk the terraces first and leave the falls for last, you have to travel wet, so another option is to swim at the end of the day and bring a change of clothes.
Start from Tagbilaran, see the Candijay terraces and waterfall, and have lunch.
Move on toward Anda and stay at a coastal lodging.
Flights run from Manila to Bohol-Panglao International Airport (TAG) and take about
1 hour 20 minutes
. Check airlines and schedules when you book.
From the airport to Tagbilaran takes about
30 minutes
by taxi or van.
Take a bus or van bound for Jagna or Ubay from the Dao terminal in Tagbilaran and get off at Candijay. A 2019 travel account says the van took over an hour and cost
, while the bus took about twice as long.
In Candijay, if you get off at Lungsoda-an or in front of the town hall, motorcycle drivers wait there. The driver's fare is reported at about
round trip, and the ride takes about
15–30 minutes
. The fare can be negotiated.
One report says that riding a motorcycle from Panglao took about
2 to 2.5 hours
(about
105 km
). There are many roads, so it is easy to get confused on a first visit.
The Bohol tourism guide says that a four-wheel-drive vehicle is recommended for private cars. An ordinary car may struggle on the last stretch.
Some day tours that combine Anda and Candijay include these terraces or the falls. Check according to your plan.
A tour has long travel times, so you may have little time at the terraces; ask in advance how much time is included.

Cadapdapan's paddies are in the mountains of eastern Bohol, so the road becomes slippery and muddy in rainy periods. One traveler recommended November to March, after the harvest, and the flow of the falls may drop in the dry season.
We could not confirm the planting and harvest seasons. If you want to see green paddies, ask locally about the timing before you go.

To see the terraces and the falls on the same day, walking the terraces in the morning and going into the water at the falls at midday is a sensible order. Buses become fewer late in the afternoon, so head back to town in good time.

Cadapdapan has no lodging of its own, so use the town center of Candijay or a coastal stay toward Anda. Most people come as a day trip from Tagbilaran or Panglao, but if an early start is hard, you can stay a night in Anda and come from there.

The farm restaurant in the middle of the paddies is the closest place to eat. We could not confirm the menu and prices, so check on site. Candijay town also has restaurants, so choose lunch to suit your schedule.
Bring plenty of cash. The small fees are all in cash and change may be short.
Walk only on the marked paths and do not step on the paddy edges or dikes.
Ask permission before taking photos where residents are present.
Wear non-slip shoes.
Agree on the route and the return time with your motorcycle driver at the start.
If you plan to swim at the falls, bring spare clothes and a towel.
Be sure to check the last bus or van time for the return trip.
Opening hours differ by source, from 8 a.m. to 5 or 6 p.m., so check locally.
Candijay is a small town of about 30,000 people as of 2024, so ATMs may be scarce. Withdraw plenty of cash in Tagbilaran before you set out.
Cadapdapan is on a remote mountain road, and it turns muddy and slippery when it rains. On rainy days it is safer to postpone your trip.
Fees differ between sources and private-land sections may be charged separately, so check locally.
There is no separate public viewpoint, and you pass through private land to see the paddies, so follow residents' guidance.
The path to the falls is very steep and slippery, so do not push yourself.
Bus and van schedules are irregular, so arrange your return transport in advance.
The information in this article reflects what could be verified as of 2026; check the latest announcements.
The paddies are residents' livelihood, so leave no trash and ask residents' permission before flying a drone.
Right near the farm is
Can-umantad Falls
, described as the highest in Bohol.
The municipality that includes Cadapdapan is
Candijay
, with mangrove forests and a sandbar.
Combined with
Anda
on the eastern coast, it makes a one- or two-day plan.
It is about

from the gateway city of
